turns.user: What layer cycle-time window do I need for a 1 m high wall, 20 mm nozzle, static yield stress 2 kPa, Athix 0.8 Pa/s, open time 45 min, starting 10 min after mixing?
turns.text:
I’ll run the buildability calculator for the wall and report the cycle-time range, including any geometry or material defaults it uses.
The calculator needs one trial cycle time to evaluate the schedule. I’ll use 30 seconds as a trial value; it will calculate the allowable window from there.
**There is no feasible layer cycle-time window** for the specified free-standing wall. The calculator requires **at least 198 s per layer** for stability, while the 45 min open time and 10 min delayed start allow **at most 21 s per layer**.

It classified the wall as **non-printable**, with free-wall buckling governing. It assumed 100 layers at 10 mm each, a 23.69 mm layer width, a single filament, density 2,100 kg/m³, and a 1.5 safety factor. At the 21 s limit, it also predicts plastic collapse near layer 20. A braced wall or multiple filaments would address the buckling check; the material and open time would still need reassessment before printing.

Calculator outputs: [assessment](</C:/Users/User/3D Printing Concrete Prediction/artifacts/reports/agent/20261016-172927-fe68/assessment_job.md>) · [cycle-time plot](</C:/Users/User/3D Printing Concrete Prediction/artifacts/reports/agent/20261016-172927-fe68/cycle_sweep_job.png>). Verify the final setup experimentally.
